top3.headline: Claude caught issues human reviewers missed in drug manufacturing documents
top3.whyItMatters: Regulated review work is where agents now show measurable time savings, with humans still checking.

top3.headline: Agent-facing web interfaces kept 91% of tested attacks exploitable
top3.whyItMatters: Review interface design before exposing systems to agents; it swung exploitability from 39% to 95%.

top3.headline: Cursor turns drawing on a web page into agent instructions
top3.whyItMatters: Non-engineers can now direct coding agents with visual edits instead of written specs.

items.title: Anthropic gives US governments 40% off Claude, no minimum spend
items.takeaway: The OneGov deal covers Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the API; Anthropic estimates $1B in savings.
items.soWhat: Steep public-sector discounts show vendors buying adoption; use them as a benchmark in your own deals.

related.name: Anthropic: Expanding our partnership with GSA

items.title: Researchers object to OpenAI gating its claimed math breakthroughs
items.takeaway: OpenAI released the Kakeya result but routes others through hand-picked expert shepherds; physics is unreleased.
items.soWhat: Big AI claims released to a chosen few are hard to verify, so treat them as unconfirmed.

items.title: Anthropic reports early drug-development gains with six partners
items.takeaway: Partners include Bristol Myers Squibb; Anthropic also bought Mithril Medicine and started its own drug programs.
items.soWhat: Claude cut one manufacturing review by 89% while catching more issues, though most work is still preclinical.

items.title: Cursor lets you prompt agents by drawing on the page
items.takeaway: Annotate in design mode: edit elements, draw, and check screen sizes; Cmd+Shift+D starts it.
items.soWhat: Designers and PMs can steer coding agents visually, shortening the handoff from mockup to code.

items.title: LangSmith now tracks LLM cache hit rates for agents
items.takeaway: Hit rate shows overall, per thread, and over time in dashboard templates.
items.soWhat: Cache hits drive agent cost, so teams now get a direct number to watch spend.

items.title: Hex rebuilds its analytics platform for agents and raises $100M
items.takeaway: Hex 4.0 is a from-scratch rewrite built on plain code; the round values Hex at $1.2B.
items.soWhat: Hex says its old agent harness bloated with hundreds of tools, so it rebuilt everything as code.

items.title: Agent-facing web interfaces let AI agents carry out known attacks
items.takeaway: 91% of 44 tested vulnerabilities stayed exploitable; interface design moved retention from 39% to 95%.
items.soWhat: How you design agent interfaces matters far more for security than which agent vendor you pick.

image.alt: arXiv: Agent-facing web interfaces let AI agents carry out known attacks

items.title: A self-improving meta agent writes skills that beat human-curated ones
items.takeaway: 60.7% pass rate on 83 SkillsBench tasks, versus 56.4% for human-curated skills.
items.soWhat: Agent skills may soon be tuned by agents, though the reported gain is modest at about four points.
